instructions: Cut the chicken thighs into 1 1/2-inch pieces and pat them dry. Put them in a large bowl.

Put the chilies, coriander seeds, cinnamon, cloves, green cardamom, black cardamom, peppercorns and mace in a wide, dry skillet over low heat. Stir for 2 minutes, until they smell toasty. Don't walk away. Burnt spices turn bitter.
Add the coconut, cumin, sesame seeds and poppy seeds. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the coconut is golden. Stir in the nutmeg, then transfer everything onto a plate and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Grind the cooled spices to a fine powder in a spice grinder or blender.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's golden at the edges.
Add the ginger and garlic, chopped. Cook for 1 minute, until the raw smell is gone. Transfer the mixture to a blender and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Add the ground spices and 2 tbsp water to the blender. Blend into a thick paste. It will be a little lumpy and oily, and that's fine.
Scrape the paste into the bowl with the chicken, add the turmeric and 3/4 tsp of the salt, and stir until every piece is coated. Leave it on the counter for 15 minutes while you start the rice.

Put the rice in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water. Bring it to a boil over high heat, cover, and turn the heat to low. Cook for 12 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.

Wipe out the skillet and heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil over medium heat. Add the tomatoes, finely chopped, with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 5 minutes, until they break down into a jammy sauce.
Add the chicken and all the paste from the bowl. Stir for 4 minutes, until the masala darkens and smells cooked.

Pour in 3/4 cup hot water and add 1/3 cup chopped cilantro. Bring it to a bubble, turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes, stirring once, until the chicken is tender and oil floats on top of the sauce.

You're cooking the thighs to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one piece there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open. It's done when there's no pink left and it pulls apart easily with a fork.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice and put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants more heat.

To keep half for later, cool it and transfer it to a closed container. It keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. Thaw frozen curry in the fridge overnight, then warm it in a covered pot over low heat with a splash of water.
method_notes: The lead (Swasthi's Recipes, 4.98 from 87) dry-roasts a long list of whole spices with coconut, sesame and poppy seeds, grinds them, and blends them with fried onion, ginger and garlic into a paste that coats the chicken before it goes into a tomato base. Yummy Tummy Aarthi's pressure cooker version and Wokme's quicker one use a similar roasted masala. This version follows the lead scaled up to 4 servings, with boneless thighs so it cooks in about 20 minutes, 4 Kashmiri chilies for a mild base, and red pepper flakes at the table for the heat Kolhapuri is known for. It is gluten-free, dairy-free and nut-free as written.
